item.title: Urgent: Failure to Empty Bins in Children's Play Area – Adams Gardens Estate, 14th October
item.description:
I would like to formally raise my concerns regarding the ongoing failure to empty the bins within the children’s play area at Adams Gardens Estate. The bins have reportedly not been emptied for over three months, resulting in a significant accumulation of rubbish. This situation is unacceptable, particularly given that the affected area is used by children and families. The prolonged build-up of waste is now creating serious concerns regarding hygiene, public health and pest control. There have been numerous reports of mice and rats in and around the estate’s bins, and the accumulation of uncollected rubbish is likely to be contributing to the problem. The presence of rodents so close to a children’s play area is particularly concerning and presents a potential health and safety risk to residents, especially young children. I am therefore requesting that Southwark Council take urgent action to address this matter by: • Arranging for the bins within the children’s play area to be emptied without further delay. • Ensuring the surrounding area is thoroughly cleaned and any accumulated waste is removed. • Arranging an appropriate pest control inspection and treatment in response to reports of mice and rats. • Reviewing the waste collection arrangements to ensure the bins are emptied regularly and this situation does not recur. Please treat this as an urgent environmental health concern and confirm what action will be taken, including the expected timescale for resolving the issue. Residents should not have to endure months of overflowing or unemptied bins, particularly in an area intended for children to play safely. I look forward to receiving your prompt response and confirmation that this matter will be addressed.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Hatteraick Road, Rotherhithe, Greater London
